title: Watchlist Architecture Addendum v2 — view-layer restructure (D38), data ownership, shared D15 locking, theme subsystem (D40)

sections.heading: View-layer restructure — component map after D38 (Portfolio replaces Month Grid; Watchlist = candidates only)
sections.body: DELTA over Watchlist_Architecture_Addendum_v1: the shell's sidebar nav becomes EXACTLY six items in fixed order — Dashboard -> /, Portfolio -> /portfolio (renamed destination of the old Month Grid), Watchlist -> /watch, Financial Goals -> /goals, Alerts -> /notifications, Settings -> /settings. The v1 nav map is superseded on two points: 'Month Grid' no longer exists as a label or destination (its route content becomes Portfolio) and the v1 'Reports/Print' sidebar item is dropped from the six-label set (its routes /print, /share, /export.csv remain served; the approved design places Share/Export under Settings). Component map: (1) Dashboard — stat tiles, charts and monthly history, unchanged data sources. (2) PORTFOLIO screen at /portfolio as a tab container: Tab A 'My Holdings' = the position registry (columns Company/ISIN, Rating, Coupon, Yield, Frequency, Invested, Received, Next Payout, Status per FR-53) carrying the Add Position entry (D39 approved location) and the per-row detail drawer; Tab B 'Payouts' = the month-grid pattern (companies x elapsed months + current month only, cells show amount or status chip, rows auto-sorted Danger -> On-going -> Matured) carrying the payment-health chips; the tab state travels in the URL (?tab=holdings|payouts, default holdings) exactly as the v1 two-view pattern did; a Status legend card (Watching/On-going/Danger/Matured) renders on Portfolio. (3) WATCHLIST screen at /watch = candidates ONLY: the FR-56 whitelist columns (Company/ISIN, Rating, Coupon, Est. Yield, Source note, Action), status Watching, + Add Candidate action and the Move to Portfolio action per row — no Invested/Received/Next Payout columns and no payment-health chips exist anywhere on this screen. (4) Financial Goals, Alerts, Settings screens keep their v1 containers. SURVIVORS: the D33 detail drawer and the D33 alerts panel (overdue / due-soon / maturity cards) both SURVIVE this restructure unchanged in behavior but are now ATTACHED TO PORTFOLIO ROWS — the drawer opens from My Holdings registry rows (and candidate rows in the drawer fragment path), and the alerts panel renders beside the Portfolio row set (alerts derive from positions, and Watchlist candidates have no payment events to alert on). Route deltas: GET /portfolio (tab param, named error on unknown tab) replaces the month-grid screen route; GET /watch keeps its route but serves only watch_state='watching' rows; POST /watch/<id>/move stays as the Move to Portfolio endpoint (action label renamed per D39); the Add Position POST lands from /portfolio. Templates: the shell partial carries the six-label nav; Portfolio templates render the tab container + both panels; the watchlist template drops its holdings half. Reuse rules from v1 remain hard: status/health from the day-wise helpers only, one shared money formatter, one parameterized query per request with a fixed sort whitelist.

sections.heading: Data ownership — positions table vs candidate store, read-time health, render-only labels
sections.body: Ownership boundaries after the D38/D39 split, all inside the module-monolith (one Flask app, one SQLite file): (1) POSITIONS (bonds rows with watch_state='holding') own every money fact — Invested is bonds.amount, Received is the paid-ledger sum over payment_ledger rows for that position, Next Payout is the earliest unpaid tenure month (amount + credit day) — and own the FR-40 display fields, dates and credit_day. The Portfolio surfaces (My Holdings registry, Payouts grid, dashboard) read these facts through the existing parameterized read model (the v3 two-view query re-pointed: its holdings half now serves Portfolio, its watching half serves the candidates-only Watchlist). (2) THE CANDIDATE STORE (bonds rows with watch_state='watching') owns watchlist rows: research fields only — company, ISIN, rating, coupon, est. yield, source note, status Watching. A candidate row owns NO payment facts by construction: it has no ledger rows, so Invested/Received/Next Payout and all payment-health values are structurally absent from the Watchlist render — the FR-56 whitelist is an ownership boundary, not a cosmetic column hide. (3) PAYMENT HEALTH (On-going/Danger/Matured) is DERIVED AT READ TIME from the Payouts grid entries — for the credit-day rule: entry present with amount > 0 on or before the credit day -> On-going; no qualifying entry once the credit day arrives -> Danger from that same day; tenure end reached -> Matured. Nothing stores health: no status column is written for it, every render recomputes from payment_ledger, and two reads over unchanged data agree (DATA-05 read-time rule; D38 owner rule 'everything reflects from the monthly grid'). The engine's own D5 status computation is untouched. (4) LABEL MAPPING exists ONLY at the render layer: the fixed mapping Returned -> Received and Completed -> Matured is applied by one template helper on every surface (registry headers, Payouts chips, drawer, dashboard, legend, print/share). Engine values, stored rows, schema names and every computation keep the original strings — a stored engine 'Completed' renders 'Matured' and the database round-trip still reads 'Completed'. CSV exports and calculations consume engine values, never display labels. Purchase state (Watching | Held) lives in watch_state and is set only by the two creation funnels (Add Position creates holding/Held; Move to Portfolio flips watching -> holding); payment health never writes it.

sections.heading: Locking — one shared D15 routine behind both Add Position and Move to Portfolio (module-monolith)
sections.body: The strict active-position lock is ONE routine used by BOTH position-creation funnels — the module-monolith shape (Flask + server-rendered/vanilla-JS front end, single SQLite store) makes this a single module function, never a second implementation: the existing lock validator (AF-39 in src/validators.py) is called by the Add Position POST handler (AF-65) and by the Move to Portfolio handler (AF-66) with identical arguments and identical semantics. Contract: match key = normalized company name (trim + case-insensitive) OR normalized ISIN (trim + uppercase); a duplicate is blocked if EITHER key matches a DIFFERENT position whose live engine status is On-going or Danger (engine Completed — displayed Matured — is excluded from the active set); the verdict is a HARD BLOCK with a named error naming the blocking position and its status ('Cannot add position: <company> has an active position (<status>)' for the form, the ERR-move-watching-shaped message for the move) — no override, no force-accept path exists in either handler. Lock RELEASE: only when the matching position reaches engine Completed (D5: months paid >= tenure) — after Matured a re-buy (Add Position) or a later move is allowed, and the new position restarts the lifecycle as On-going/Danger, re-locking the company until it too completes (FR-57 re-buy clause). Enforcement point: SERVER-SIDE inside both POST handlers before any write — the browser UI is never the enforcement (client JS may hide the button; the handler still runs the check), so zero writes occur on every block. The move additionally validates the mandatory position fields (amount, dates, credit_day 1..31) BEFORE the lock, preserving the v1 rule that a candidate with holes can never become a position. The lock runs on every submit — there is no add-time-only or move-time-only shortcut; the invariant 'at most one active position per company' holds continuously across the watch_state boundary. Architecture diagram impact: the route_handlers node gains /portfolio (Add Position inside it) and re-points POST /watch/<id>/move; both edges converge on the single validators/lock node — no new table, no schema change for locking (D15 works over bonds + live status).

sources: docs/Atomic_Functions_addendum_v4.json (AF-65, AF-66 — both call the shared routine)

sections.heading: Theme subsystem — token sets, data-theme, System via prefers-color-scheme, localStorage, pre-paint bootstrap (D40)
sections.body: Three shipped themes — System (follows OS), Light (default), Dark — implemented WITHOUT a framework and WITHOUT external assets (offline rule; system font stack only). (1) TOKEN LAYER: every color on every screen comes from CSS custom properties in exactly two token blocks — light tokens on :root (the approved v4 palette: bg/card/text/muted/border/accent + status chip foreground/background pairs) and dark tokens on html[data-theme=dark] (near-black #111827-family surfaces, desaturated accents, WCAG AA contrast pairs, NO pure #000000 or #ffffff surface anywhere). Component stylesheets reference var() only; a color literal outside the two token blocks is a defect (TC-111 greps for it). (2) data-theme ATTRIBUTE: the resolved token set rides on the html root — data-theme='light' or 'dark' for explicit modes; mode System carries NO explicit data-theme, so the @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) block (scoped to apply only when no explicit data-theme is present) resolves tokens — which makes OS-following live with zero JavaScript, while explicit Light/Dark unconditionally override the OS. (3) PERSISTENCE: the user's mode (system|light|dark) is stored in localStorage under 'theme_mode' — browser-local only, deliberately NOT an alert_prefs key (D40 chose localStorage; no server round trip, nothing to sync). Fresh install has no key -> Light default. (4) PRE-PAINT BOOTSTRAP: an inline vanilla-JS snippet in the document <head>, before the stylesheet and body, reads 'theme_mode' synchronously and sets/clears data-theme before the first paint — saved Dark never shows a Light frame and vice versa (zero-flash); storage failure falls back to Light with no crash. (5) SURFACES: a three-way switcher in the header (global chrome) plus a Settings > Appearance section — both render the same System/Light/Dark options and stay in sync through the one apply/persist/restore path; the switcher is the only theme control the app ships. (6) OFFLINE/NO-FRAMEWORK CONSTRAINT: no theme library, no CDN, no icon font, no runtime fetch — the entire subsystem is two CSS blocks, one attribute and one small inline script (D40 community pattern: shadcn-style CSS-variable tokens, MDN prefers-color-scheme, localStorage persistence). Theme state never touches the database, exports or print styling logic beyond re-resolving the same tokens.
